newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea agrees to aid talks with North in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea agrees to aid talks with North in Beijing.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross will accept its North Korean counterpart's suggestion that talks on speeding up food aid be held in Beijing, Seoul government officials said on Tuesday.

The southern side earlier this month proposed the talks be held in the border village of Panmunjom but North Korea's Red Cross, after it welcomed the proposal, insisted discussions be held in Beijing on May 3.
"Government officials agreed that the talks should take place in view of difficulties in the North," an official said after a meeting with representatives of the southern Red Cross.
"The acceptance on the venue will be notified to the North soon," he added.
Although the Red Cross is authorised to deliver private-level food to North Korea, the Seoul government makes policy decisions on all contacts with the communist state.
International aid groups have said North Korea, hit hard by devastating floods for two years in a row, is sliding into famine with reports of deaths of children from malnutrition.
Last week the South Korean side said there was no need for Koreans to meet in a third country and proposed a working-level session in Panmunjom on Tuesday.
On Monday, the North Korean Red Cross reiterated its position in a message relayed via a telephone hot-line at Panmunjom.

The South Korean Red Cross, which has sent 16 shipments of food and garments to its northern counterpart, plans to ship 110 tonnes of wheat flour, worth 36 million won ($40,300), to the North later this week, Red Cross officials said.
The wheat flour was bought with money raised by a South Korean Christian group.
The two Koreas remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
